stem: What is a purpose of Cisco AI PODs?
explanation: Cisco AI PODs provide a prevalidated, integrated full-stack infrastructure platform for enterprise artificial intelligence. Cisco describes AI PODs as combining Cisco UCS compute, Cisco Nexus networking, accelerated GPUs, enterprise storage, management, orchestration, and supporting software into an architecture designed for the complete AI workload lifecycle. The supported workload spectrum explicitly includes model training, fine-tuning, and high-throughput inference. Option D therefore captures both the architectural scope and workload intent. The principal value of AI POD is that organizations do not need to independently design and validate every server, accelerator, network, storage, and software dependency. Cisco supplies validated designs and modular scale-unit architectures that accelerate deployment while retaining enterprise operational characteristics. Option A is too restrictive because AI POD is not merely cloud-native lifecycle software and its hardware scope extends far beyond compute. Option B incorrectly makes inferencing the primary focus; Cisco AI POD supports the complete AI lifecycle and can be purpose-built for training, inference, or mixed workloads. Option C understates the architecture by describing it merely as modular hardware components. Cisco explicitly characterizes AI POD as an integrated full-stack solution. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Components and Architecture — Cisco AI infrastructure solutions, compute, networking, storage, GPU acceleration, and scalable architectures.

stem: A data center facility experienced a power outage, and the UCS X-Series servers did not restart automatically when power is restored. The configuration must be updated to prioritize these servers to boot as soon as possible to resume their work. Which set of power policy configurations must be used to meet these requirements?
explanation: Two settings determine the required behavior. First, Power Restore must be configured as Always On . Cisco defines this setting as instructing the server to power on after power is restored following a loss event. Immediate is not one of the documented Power Restore states; supported states include Last State, Always On, and Always Off. Second, Power Priority should be High . Cisco explains that Power Priority determines initial power allocation among servers. A server assigned a higher priority receives preference when power is being allocated, which directly supports the requirement that these systems restart as soon as possible. Cisco validated designs explicitly show Power Profiling enabled with Power Priority set to High for performance- oriented deployments. Power Profiling permits the platform to determine server power requirements. The Processor Package Power Limit should remain at Default for the X-Series scenario. Cisco documentation also notes that the selectable PPL setting is specifically applicable to particular C225/C245 M8 systems rather than being the mechanism for prioritizing X-Series restart behavior. Option C provides Always On but fails to assign High power priority. Options A and D contain the invalid Immediate restore setting. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — UCS power management, recovery after power loss, power prioritization, and infrastructure availability.

stem: A network engineer analyzes RoCEv2 traffic flows in an AI training cluster and notices that all RoCEv2 packets have the Don’t Fragment bit set in the IP header. Why must RoCEv2 set the DF bit in all packets?
explanation: RoCEv2 transports the InfiniBand transport protocol over UDP/IP, allowing RDMA traffic to traverse Layer 3 networks. The RDMA transport layer preserves packet-level sequencing, reliability, and ordering semantics that are inappropriate for arbitrary IP fragmentation. Consequently, RoCEv2 traffic is designed to traverse the network without IP fragmentation, making option D the intended technical answer. NVIDIA documentation confirms that RoCEv2 places the InfiniBand transport protocol behind UDP and IP rather than using the native InfiniBand network-layer header. A consistent end-to-end MTU is therefore essential in GPU fabrics. AI clusters commonly use jumbo frames, and every switch interface, port channel, Layer 3 interface, and server NIC along the path must support the configured packet size. Unexpected fragmentation is incompatible with the deterministic behavior required by high-performance RDMA workloads. Option A identifies a general IPv4 consequence of setting DF—Path MTU Discovery can use DF—but it is not the fundamental RoCE transport requirement tested here. Option B is incorrect because DF does not classify packets as RDMA. Option C is also incorrect because ECMP path selection is normally determined by packet-header hashing; the DF flag does not force packets onto a single path. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Deployment and Data Management — RoCEv2, MTU design, lossless transport, and high-performance Ethernet.

to indicate to intermediate switches that the packet contains RDMA traffic requiring special handling
to ensure that packets always take the same path through ECMP routing for consistent latency
to prevent IP fragmentation that would break the InfiniBand sequence numbering and ordering guarantees

stem: Which set of statements describes Quantized Congestion Notification?
explanation: Data Center Quantized Congestion Notification, or DCQCN, combines ECN-based end-to-end congestion signaling with Priority Flow Control to maintain efficient and effectively lossless RoCE transport. Cisco states that ECN reacts first , while PFC functions as a safety mechanism if congestion escalates faster than endpoint rate control can respond. With moderate queue buildup, WRED marks ECN-capable packets. If queue utilization continues toward critical levels, PFC pauses the affected priority before packet loss occurs. The second statement in option C is also correct. When the receiving host receives a RoCEv2 packet carrying the ECN Congestion Experienced marking, the receiving endpoint generates a Congestion Notification Packet, or CNP, toward the transmitting source. The source then reduces its transmission rate according to the congestion-control algorithm. The network switch performs the ECN marking but does not generate the RoCE CNP on behalf of the receiver. This eliminates options A, B, and D. Options A and D additionally reverse the normal operational sequence by claiming that PFC responds before ECN. The distinction is important because efficient AI fabrics seek to manage congestion proactively through ECN while reserving PFC for severe congestion and microbursts. Study Guide Reference: 3.1.a Congestion control mechanisms — PFC and ECN; 3.1.b RoCEv2.

stem: Which function is provided through natural language processing?
explanation: Natural language processing enables computer systems to interpret, analyze, transform, and generate human language. It operates on textual or spoken language and is foundational to applications such as speech recognition, transcription, conversational assistants, document intelligence, summarization, sentiment analysis, and information extraction. Consequently, converting human speech or written material into machine-processable, structured information is the function that best represents NLP in this question. Cisco describes NLP-oriented technologies in its collaboration platforms through natural-language understanding, speech-to-text, transcription, translation, conversational AI, and question-answering capabilities. Cisco's AI workforce material also associates NLP engineering with text understanding, speech- to-text AI, semantic search, and language models. Option A is a storage and compression function. Option C relates to networking, protocol processing, and authorization rather than natural-language interpretation. Option D represents data cleansing or deduplication and does not specifically require NLP. Within the DCAI blueprint, this capability falls under the broader requirement to understand AI use cases and AI workload characteristics. The essential distinction is that NLP operates on human language and converts linguistic information into representations that applications can process programmatically. Study Guide Reference: 1.0 AI Fundamentals and Applications — 1.3 Describe AI use cases.

stem: A customer deploys a UCS 885a server in a data center with two power grids. Three of the 3000W power supplies in the server connect to each grid. Due to an external event, one of the grids will be shut down for maintenance. How does the server respond to this event?
explanation: The Cisco UCS C885A M8 contains six 3000-W 54-V AC power supplies and normally supports an N+2 power configuration . In the scenario, three PSUs are connected to each independent power grid. Losing one complete grid therefore leaves only three operational 54-V PSUs. Cisco's installation and service documentation specifies the resulting behavior precisely: when only three 54- V AC PSUs remain available, the server continues operating but enters a reduced-performance condition in which power to each GPU is capped at 60 percent . Cisco further states that four or more 54-V power supplies allow operation at full performance. Consequently, the system does not immediately shut down, eliminating option A. A graceful operating-system shutdown is also not automatically initiated, eliminating D. Option C is incorrect because three active supplies are insufficient for full-performance operation on this platform. This behavior allows the server to remain available during a significant power-domain failure while keeping its consumption within the capacity of the remaining PSUs. The operational tradeoff is reduced accelerator performance until adequate power redundancy is restored. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — UCS C885A M8 power redundancy, degraded operation, GPU power management, and availability.

stem: A customer uses Cisco AI Products within Intersight and observes packet drops for RoCEv2 traffic. Which System QoS policy configuration must be deployed to ensure that RoCEv2 traffic is classified as lossless?
explanation: RoCEv2 traffic must be mapped to a no-drop QoS class when lossless Ethernet operation is required. Cisco's current Intersight VIC configuration guidance provides an explicit configuration for this requirement: create a System QoS policy, select Platinum as the priority, and clear the Allow Packet Drops checkbox. The policy is then associated with the UCS Domain Profile. Cisco's storage best-practice documentation gives the same configuration for NVMe over RoCEv2: Platinum enabled, Allow Packet Drops unchecked, and a jumbo MTU—commonly 9216 at the system-class level. This establishes the UCS-side no-drop class required for RDMA traffic. Disabling Platinum, as proposed in option A, would remove the intended lossless traffic class. Enabling every system class in option B does not automatically make RoCEv2 lossless because packet-drop behavior remains a property of the selected class. Disabling Gold in option C is unrelated to ensuring that the RoCE traffic class receives no-drop treatment. A complete RoCE design must maintain consistent QoS classification and no-drop handling end to end. However, for the System QoS policy requested here, option D is the precise Cisco configuration. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Deployment and Data Management — RoCEv2, PFC, lossless Ethernet, and UCS System QoS.

stem: When considering a rail-only network design, when would adding spine switches make sense?
explanation: A rail-optimized architecture is intentionally designed so that communication among corresponding GPU ranks within a single scalable unit can remain on the rail or leaf switches. This provides single-hop forwarding and avoids unnecessary traversal through spine switches, reducing latency for collective communication. Spines become necessary when the deployment expands beyond one scalable unit. Cisco explicitly documents that multiple scalable units can be interconnected through leaf-and-spine switching. Traffic among GPUs inside one scalable unit benefits from rail-optimized single-hop communication, whereas traffic between GPUs located in different scalable units traverses the spine layer. Therefore, option C precisely describes when spine switches provide architectural value: scaling the AI fabric beyond the boundaries of one scalable unit . Option A is inaccurate because the rail design already provides the required local GPU bandwidth within the scalable unit; adding spines is not primarily intended to increase local rail bandwidth. Option B mischaracterizes the principal design purpose. Although additional topology can contribute to resiliency, spines are introduced fundamentally for interconnecting scalable units and enabling scale-out. Option D is also incorrect because increased buffering is not the architectural reason for introducing a spine tier. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Components and Architecture — rail-optimized topology, scalable units, nonblocking network design, latency, and horizontal scaling.

stem: An engineer is deploying a Cisco AI POD environment to support large-scale AI workloads. The solution must provide a software-defined storage platform with a Disaggregated Shared-Everything architecture, allow compute nodes to run on Cisco UCS C225 M8 servers managed through Cisco Intersight, and deliver exabyte- scale, all-flash performance with integrated high-speed RDMA and GPU Direct Storage capabilities. Which solution meets the requirements?
explanation: VAST Data Universal Storage is the architecture explicitly associated with these requirements. Cisco's AI Data Platform documentation describes VAST's Disaggregated Shared-Everything (DASE) architecture, which separates stateless compute from persistent flash capacity so that storage performance and capacity can scale independently. This architecture is designed to eliminate conventional storage-controller bottlenecks and support extremely large AI datasets. Cisco's AI POD with VAST architecture integrates Cisco UCS infrastructure, Cisco Intersight lifecycle management, high-performance Ethernet/RDMA networking, and VAST's all-flash storage platform. Cisco documentation also identifies UCS C225 M8 systems within VAST-based storage designs and describes the solution as optimized for high-throughput AI workloads. GPU Direct Storage is particularly important because it reduces unnecessary CPU involvement and intermediate data copies when transferring datasets between storage and GPU memory. Combined with RDMA, this architecture can sustain the high parallel bandwidth required by large training and fine-tuning environments. NetApp AFF and Pure Storage FlashBlade are capable enterprise storage products, but the DASE terminology uniquely identifies VAST. Local NVMe cannot provide the required exabyte-scale shared-storage architecture and would fragment datasets across individual GPU servers. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Components and Architecture — high-performance storage, AI PODs, RDMA, scale, and shared AI data platforms.

stem: A network operations team deploys HyperFabric AI and wants to monitor fabric health to proactively identify performance issues. The team must track metrics specifically relevant to AI training workloads. Which metric is most critical for identifying congestion issues that could impact AI training performance in a HyperFabric AI deployment?
explanation: The PFC pause-frame transmission rate per interface is the most directly relevant congestion indicator for an AI training fabric carrying RoCEv2 traffic. Priority Flow Control protects lossless traffic classes by transmitting pause frames when a receiving interface or switch queue approaches a congestion threshold. An elevated or sustained PFC pause rate therefore indicates that the lossless RDMA traffic class is repeatedly encountering queue pressure. This is particularly significant for distributed AI training. GPU collective operations require synchronized communication between large numbers of accelerators, and excessive congestion can create tail latency, reduce effective network throughput, and extend Job Completion Time. Cisco AI networking guidance consequently treats PFC, ECN, queue occupancy, drops, and congestion telemetry as key operational signals for AI backend fabrics. Spanning-tree topology changes are largely irrelevant in a modern routed or VXLAN-EVPN AI backend. BGP EVPN route counts are useful for control-plane capacity assessment but do not directly reveal congestion. VXLAN encapsulation rates measure traffic volume rather than whether buffers are becoming saturated. PFC should not be interpreted as inherently problematic—some pause activity may occur during microbursts. However, unusually high or persistent pause-frame rates are a strong signal that congestion behavior requires investigation. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — RoCEv2 monitoring, PFC, congestion, telemetry, and AI training performance.

stem: What does workload distribution offer in an AI infrastructure with local and external resources?
explanation: When an AI environment contains both local and external resources, workload distribution enables computational jobs to be placed or divided across multiple locations according to performance, capacity, latency, data residency, security, and cost requirements. This is a defining capability of hybrid AI infrastructure rather than an isolation mechanism. Cisco defines hybrid AI infrastructure as combining on-premises and cloud resources within a common operating model. Workloads can use cloud capacity for burst training or experimentation while sensitive data or steady inference operations remain on premises. Cisco further identifies workload mobility, secure connectivity, and data synchronization as explicit requirements for hybrid AI deployment in DCAI objective 2.5. Cisco material on AI workload orchestration likewise describes workload execution across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. Option A unnecessarily isolates functions rather than distributing them. Option C contradicts hybrid automation by restricting operations locally. Option D describes security-policy enforcement, which is important but does not define workload distribution. Accordingly, B is the technically correct response. It also corrects the answer indicated in the supplied source document, which lists C despite Cisco's current hybrid-infrastructure guidance. Study Guide Reference: 1.0 AI Fundamentals and Applications — 1.4.b Hybrid; 2.5 Hybrid AI deployment and workload mobility.

stem: Server administrators receive reports of power utilization being near capacity across multiple UCS X-Series servers in the data center after a hardware upgrade. The chassis operates with six power supply units in redundant power mode. How can the administrator use additional power without impacting redundancy?
explanation: Extended Power Capacity is specifically designed to increase usable power in a Cisco UCS X-Series chassis while the chassis remains configured in a redundant power mode. Cisco states that enabling Extended Power Capacity permits the chassis to borrow power capacity from the supplies reserved for redundancy, thereby increasing the total power that can be allocated to workloads. Cisco provides a six-PSU example in Grid redundancy mode. Without Extended Power Capacity, the workload is capped at 8,400 W. Enabling the feature increases the available workload capacity to approximately 9,660 W—an increase of 15 percent—while retaining the configured redundant power mode. Power capping in option A would restrict consumption rather than make additional power available. Adding more PSUs is impossible when the chassis already contains its supported complement of six supplies. Disabling Extended Power Capacity would reduce rather than increase the available power envelope. This feature is particularly useful after installing additional accelerator, PCIe, memory, or compute resources that raise chassis power demand. It should nevertheless be applied within the data center's electrical and thermal design limits. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — UCS X-Series chassis power policy, redundancy, Extended Power Capacity, and capacity management.

stem: An engineer made changes to the corporate DNS, which caused a Cisco UCS X-Series domain to lose connectivity to Intersight. To restore connectivity, the management interface DNS and NTP settings must be updated using the device console UI. Which configuration change must be made in Intersight to allow the updated DNS configuration to persist?
explanation: In an Intersight Managed Mode UCS domain, DNS and NTP configuration is policy-controlled through the UCS Domain Profile deployed to the Fabric Interconnects. Changes entered locally through the Device Console can restore temporary reachability, but the policy configuration maintained by Intersight remains authoritative. If the Domain Profile still contains the previous DNS or NTP configuration, a subsequent deployment can overwrite the locally modified values. Cisco documents that the Domain Profile references both the Network Connectivity Policy , which contains DNS settings, and the NTP Policy , which defines the NTP servers. The appropriate persistent remediation is therefore to edit the configuration associated with the deployed Domain Profile and redeploy it. The IMC Access Policy applies primarily to server-management addressing and access rather than Fabric Interconnect DNS/NTP persistence. A Device Connector policy does not supply these domain DNS settings. Option C incorrectly applies a Network Connectivity Policy to the blade chassis; for the Fabric Interconnect domain, the relevant network-connectivity configuration is referenced through the UCS Domain Profile. Cisco also advises that DNS and NTP should be configured on the management interface rather than being treated as Device Connector settings. stem: An engineer configures quality of service in the Cisco ACI fabric to connect VAST storage servers. Which combination of attributes must be selected?
explanation: Cisco's validated guidance for connecting VAST Data storage through an ACI fabric explicitly configures the RDMA storage class with Weighted Random Early Detection and Congestion Notification enabled . This makes option A directly consistent with Cisco's documented configuration. In Cisco's VAST Data ACI design example, storage traffic arrives marked with DSCP 26 and is assigned to the Level2 QoS class. PFC is enabled for the corresponding no-drop DSCP, bandwidth is reserved for storage traffic, the congestion algorithm is configured as WRED, and congestion notification is enabled. WRED and ECN-style congestion notification work together to detect developing queue pressure before buffers overflow. Rather than waiting for tail-drop conditions, the network can mark congestion-capable traffic so RoCEv2 endpoints reduce their transmission rates. PFC provides the complementary no-drop behavior when congestion becomes sufficiently severe. Option B disables the required congestion signaling. Options C and D use Tail Drop, which Cisco's documented VAST RDMA storage class does not use. stem: A bank is planning to deploy an AI inference solution at its branch locations. The solution must support workloads that require a balance of compute, memory, and potential GPU acceleration, and it must be suitable for installation by nontechnical onsite resources. The requirements are: high availability of the chassis management plane. support for up to 768 GB of memory for in-memory model storage and processing remote server launch requiring no on-site IT staff use of Cisco Intersight for SaaS-based infrastructure lifecycle management Which solution meets the requirements?
explanation: Cisco Unified Edge directly matches the distributed branch deployment requirements. The Cisco UCS XE9305 chassis contains two Unified Edge Management Controllers, providing redundancy for the chassis management plane. Its XE130c M8 compute node supports up to 768 GB of memory , precisely matching the stated in-memory processing requirement, and supports optional GPU acceleration. Operationally, Unified Edge is designed for highly distributed sites where qualified IT personnel may not be present. Cisco documents remote server launch with no onsite IT staff, zero-touch provisioning, fleet visibility, and automated lifecycle management through Cisco Intersight. Intersight provides SaaS-based infrastructure lifecycle operations across distributed Unified Edge systems. Although X-Series Direct is also suitable for remote locations, the exact combination of dual management controllers, 768-GB memory capacity, remote server launch, and Unified Edge's edge-focused lifecycle capabilities uniquely identifies option C. C845A M8 and C240 rack servers provide substantial compute capabilities but do not match the integrated edge chassis and zero-touch operational model required by the scenario. This is a classic DCAI compute-selection question in which architectural and operational requirements must be evaluated together rather than selecting solely by raw compute performance. stem: A solutions architect must implement a monitoring strategy for a new AI/ML data center infrastructure built on Cisco UCS X-Series servers with NVIDIA H100 GPUs, managed by Cisco Intersight. The main objectives are to gain deep visibility into GPU performance, identify resource bottlenecks for AI training workloads, and ensure the overall health and efficiency of the compute environment. Which Cisco Intersight capability is most critical for effectively monitoring this AI-centric infrastructure?
explanation: Cisco Intersight provides comprehensive infrastructure monitoring that extends beyond conventional CPU and memory health reporting to AI accelerator visibility and performance telemetry . Cisco's current Intersight material specifically highlights GPU performance visibility, resource-utilization trends, power consumption, device health, and Metrics Explorer as important capabilities for managing AI-ready infrastructure. This makes option D the only answer that addresses all three requirements: direct GPU visibility, detection of resource bottlenecks, and overall compute health. Monitoring GPU utilization, memory consumption, power, and associated platform telemetry allows operators to determine whether an AI workload is constrained by the GPU itself or by supporting compute, memory, networking, storage, or thermal infrastructure. Option A incorrectly characterizes an Intersight Analyze capability as an AI container and Kubernetes deployment engine. Option B identifies valuable complementary network telemetry through Nexus Dashboard, but the question asks specifically for the most critical Intersight capability for monitoring GPU- centric UCS infrastructure. Option C is contradicted by current Cisco capabilities because Intersight provides AI-accelerator and GPU-performance visibility rather than being restricted to basic CPU and memory telemetry. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — Cisco Intersight health monitoring, GPU telemetry, resource utilization, bottleneck identification, and AI infrastructure optimization.

stem: A global enterprise is deploying a new AI-driven analytics platform that requires high-performance GPU acceleration, large memory capacity, and robust virtualization support. The compute and GPU resources selected must provide direct GPU to GPU access leveraging NVLink technology. Which set of products meets the requirements?
explanation: The Cisco UCS C885A M8 with NVIDIA H200 GPUs is purpose-built for dense accelerated computing and directly satisfies the NVLink requirement. Cisco's C885A M8 NVIDIA configuration supports eight H100 or H200 SXM Tensor Core GPUs on an HGX platform. Those GPUs are interconnected using NVIDIA NVLink, providing the high-bandwidth GPU-to-GPU communication necessary for distributed tensor processing inside the server. The platform also provides substantial host-memory capacity, dual AMD EPYC processors, high-speed local NVMe storage, multiple 400-GbE adapters for inter-node GPU communication, and Cisco Intersight integration. These capabilities make it appropriate for large language models, generative AI training, fine- tuning, RAG, and large inference workloads. Option A does not provide the same HGX NVLink-based eight-GPU architecture with an L40 configuration. Option B uses AMD accelerators; AMD GPU connectivity employs AMD interconnect technologies rather than NVIDIA NVLink. Option C is designed for materially different workload and GPU-density requirements and does not deliver the HGX H200 NVLink topology specified by the scenario. The critical selection criterion is not merely whether a server can host a discrete GPU. The question explicitly requires direct GPU-to-GPU access through NVLink , which identifies the NVIDIA HGX-based C885A M8 configuration. stem: Which IP-based storage transport supports flow control between directly connected devices?
explanation: NVMe over RoCE uses Remote Direct Memory Access over Converged Ethernet and can employ Priority Flow Control (PFC) to provide lossless behavior between directly connected Ethernet devices. PFC is a link- level IEEE 802.1Qbb mechanism: a congested interface can transmit pause frames for a specific priority to its directly connected upstream peer. This allows the RoCE traffic class to pause without stopping unrelated Ethernet classes. Cisco's current Intersight guidance for NVMe over RoCEv2 explicitly requires a consistent no-drop class across the network. Cisco recommends enabling the Platinum QoS class, disabling packet drops for that class, and using jumbo MTU values for NVMe/RoCE traffic. NVMe/TCP and iSCSI operate over conventional TCP/IP. TCP provides end-to-end transport reliability and congestion control, but these protocols do not depend on PFC-based lossless Ethernet between adjacent devices. Fibre Channel has its own native credit-based flow-control mechanisms, but it is not an IP-based storage transport, eliminating option D. The key distinction is therefore the combination of IP transport, RDMA, and Ethernet priority-based link flow control , which identifies NVMe/RoCE. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Components and Architecture — storage technologies including NVMe; high-performance storage networking and RoCE.

stem: A customer is deploying a new AI fabric with all new NVIDIA GPUs and must verify the performance between the nodes in the network. Which tool must be used to validate the customer benchmarks?
explanation: NVIDIA Collective Communications Library (NCCL) is the appropriate framework for validating communication performance between NVIDIA GPU nodes. NCCL provides highly optimized implementations of collective operations such as AllReduce, AllGather, Reduce, Broadcast, and ReduceScatter. These operations closely represent the communication patterns generated by distributed AI training and therefore provide much more meaningful validation of GPU-cluster performance than conventional network-throughput tests. NCCL-based benchmarks can reveal whether GPU-to-GPU communication is achieving expected bandwidth and latency across NVLink, PCIe, and the external backend network. They are particularly useful when validating RoCEv2 fabrics because distributed training performance depends on collective communication efficiency rather than simple host-to-host TCP throughput. iPerf measures conventional TCP or UDP network performance between hosts and is useful for basic network validation, but it does not exercise NVIDIA GPU collective communications. Spirent and Ixia provide sophisticated packet-generation and network-testing platforms, yet they test the network primarily from a packet-forwarding perspective rather than measuring actual GPU collective-operation behavior. For a newly deployed NVIDIA AI cluster, NCCL benchmarking therefore provides workload-representative validation of the end-to-end GPU communication architecture and can expose problems involving topology, NIC configuration, congestion control, bandwidth imbalance, or fabric design. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — performance benchmarking, NVIDIA GPU communications, backend-fabric validation, and distributed AI workload testing.

stem: An engineer must configure dynamic load balancing (DLB) on a Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch AI fabric using a CLI. Which configuration must be implemented for only the odd-numbered interfaces?
explanation: Cisco NX-OS configures interface-specific Dynamic Load Balancing through the DLB hardware profile , not independently under each physical interface. Therefore, option C most accurately describes the required configuration: create or enter the DLB hardware profile and provide the selected interface list. Cisco also notes that changes to this interface list generally require a switch reload before they become effective. Option A incorrectly implies that dlb-interface is applied in standard interface configuration mode. It is actually configured under the hardware profile dlb submode. Option B describes policy-driven DLB, which is a separate mechanism requiring QoS classification with set dlb mode; it is unnecessary when the requirement is simply to enable DLB on a predetermined set of interfaces. Option D reverses the logic and would not enable the requested interfaces. Correction: the uploaded file marks A , but current Cisco NX-OS configuration documentation supports C as written. stem: An end customer plans to deploy an AI fabric in a new data center. Their engineers are more familiar with CLI-based networks and require the capability to automate standardized configuration templates and monitor flows for the fabric. Which data center automation tool meets the requirements?
explanation: Cisco Nexus Dashboard is the appropriate platform for operating and automating Cisco Nexus-based data center fabrics while retaining an NX-OS/CLI-oriented architecture. Nexus Dashboard Fabric Controller provides centralized provisioning, configuration management, automation, templates, monitoring, and lifecycle functions for Nexus fabrics. Cisco explicitly describes NDFC as the comprehensive automation and management platform for Cisco Nexus and MDS infrastructure. The template requirement is also directly supported. Nexus Dashboard allows policies and configuration templates to be defined centrally and deployed consistently to one or multiple fabrics. For flow visibility, Nexus Dashboard can collect fabric telemetry and reconstruct traffic paths, including packets, drops, anomalies, and flow behavior across multiple switches. Cisco Catalyst Center—formerly DNA Center—is primarily associated with enterprise campus and access networks rather than Nexus data center AI fabrics. Intersight specializes in compute and infrastructure lifecycle management, particularly UCS. Hyperfabric provides highly automated cloud-managed networking but deliberately abstracts much of the conventional CLI-centric operational model. Nexus Dashboard therefore best satisfies both requirements: standardized network automation and detailed fabric-flow monitoring while remaining aligned with traditional Nexus operational practices. stem: An engineer deploys an AI fabric on Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches connected to Cisco UCS nodes with NVIDIA GPUs. The requirements call for optimal network performance for training workloads. Adaptive routing is enabled on the NICs, and per-packet load balancing is enabled on the switches. Which other configuration must be implemented for this integration to be fully operational?
explanation: Cisco Nexus 9000 integration with NVIDIA adaptive-routing capabilities requires the Nexus switch to enable the Spectrum-X hardware profile . Cisco's current NX-OS configuration guide explicitly specifies the global configuration command hardware profile spectrum-x to enable NVIDIA Spectrum-X adaptive routing. When a Nexus switch peers with a supported NVIDIA NIC, this capability allows the NIC to handle packet reordering created by granular techniques such as per-packet Dynamic Load Balancing. This is particularly important for AI training because large synchronized RDMA flows can create uneven utilization under conventional hash-based ECMP. Cisco explains that per-packet DLB can spray packets over multiple paths and that NVIDIA adaptive routing/direct data placement enables the receiver to correctly handle packets that arrive out of order, improving utilization and collective-operation performance. Option A is not the documented NX-OS configuration syntax. Option B is not the Cisco-prescribed Nexus integration command. Option D may be relevant to traffic classification in other designs but does not activate Spectrum-X adaptive-routing interoperability. Therefore, the Cisco-documented configuration is C. This differs from the supplied file's marked answer B. Study Guide Reference: 3.0 AI Infrastructure Deployment and Data Management — 3.1.d Load distribution.

The uploaded question specifically maps the 96-GPU requirement to the Small AI Cluster , and its source answer is A. stem: A server administrator must monitor the performance and utilization of GPUs in Cisco UCS servers running AI workloads. Which two metrics must be used in Cisco Intersight to accomplish these goals? (Choose two.)
explanation: GPU Utilization and GPU Performance are the two choices that directly measure the behavior of accelerator resources used by AI workloads. GPU utilization indicates how actively the accelerator's computational resources are being consumed. Persistent low utilization can expose CPU, storage, networking, synchronization, or workload-scheduling bottlenecks, while sustained high utilization generally indicates effective use of expensive GPU capacity. Cisco Intersight is increasingly oriented toward AI-specific infrastructure visibility. Cisco states that Intersight provides actionable metrics for GPU performance , resource-utilization trends, and power efficiency. Its Metrics Explorer and monitoring capabilities provide deep telemetry for infrastructure resources, including AI accelerators. Explorer and Monitor in options B and C represent interfaces or functional capabilities rather than the performance metrics requested by the question. System CPU Utilization is useful when determining whether a workload is host-CPU constrained, but it does not directly measure GPU performance or GPU utilization. Accordingly, A and D are the two choices that correspond most directly to the stated objective of measuring GPU performance and utilization. stem: Refer to the exhibit. Users report delayed response times and network latency when running certain AI workloads on a specific Cisco UCS Intersight Managed Mode Domain. Based on the fault message and reported symptoms, which troubleshooting action must be taken first to address the network latency issues?
explanation: The exhibit reports etherErrStats rcvDelta for switch-B/slot-1/switch-ether/port-11 and shows that the receive- error delta has exceeded the configured threshold. This is a physical Ethernet interface error condition on Fabric Interconnect B, port 11. The first troubleshooting action should therefore target the Layer 1 components associated with that port . Cisco troubleshooting guidance for Fabric Interconnect interfaces recommends checking the physical layer when interfaces report errors or bad packets, including verifying that transceivers are functioning correctly, cabling is intact, and optics are compatible. This establishes option C as the appropriate first action. Option A begins at the application and compute layers even though the fault identifies a network-interface receive-error condition. Option B examines port-channel configuration, but the alarm identifies physical port 11 rather than a logical port-channel state problem. Option D would be appropriate when PFC congestion or excessive pause behavior is indicated; the exhibit instead reports Ethernet receive errors. A disciplined troubleshooting sequence begins with the fault domain explicitly identified by telemetry. Physical errors should be eliminated before higher-layer QoS, port-channel, or application analysis is undertaken. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — UCS network faults, interface telemetry, physical-layer troubleshooting, and network performance analysis.

To simplify management, configuration, and deployment of the workloads, a Cisco Intersight feature must be used that enables workload deployment at scale. explanation: Cisco Intersight Fleet Management is designed specifically for large numbers of geographically distributed systems where infrastructure and workloads must be deployed consistently across remote sites. stem: A national law firm is deploying a RAG solution for their legal research team to more efficiently use their 50 TB of confidential data and documents when preparing new contracts and briefs. They decided on a UCS X- Series chassis equipped with four GPUs and six X210c servers. Which storage solution fits this deployment?
explanation: An IP-based shared storage array is the appropriate architecture for a RAG environment containing approximately 50 TB of enterprise documents. RAG requires compute nodes to access a common body of source documents, embeddings, vector indexes, model artifacts, and intermediate datasets. With six UCS X210c servers participating in the solution, centralized shared storage avoids creating isolated data silos on individual compute nodes and allows the full AI cluster to access the same authoritative dataset. Cisco AI POD and RAG architectures use enterprise shared storage connected through high-speed Ethernet. Cisco validates IP-based protocols including NFS, iSCSI, NVMe/TCP, and—in higher-performance AI platforms—RDMA-capable storage designs. Cisco's RAG architecture with FlexPod, for example, uses NFS, iSCSI, and NVMe/TCP storage networks, while Cisco AI PODs support external storage from partners such as NetApp, Pure Storage, and VAST Data. JBOD and RAID 5 local storage remain tied to individual servers and do not provide the desired shared data layer. Tape provides economical archival retention but lacks the random-access latency and throughput required for active RAG retrieval. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Components and Architecture — storage selection, AI data access, scalability, RAG infrastructure, and shared storage.

stem: To support growing AI workload requirements, a regional medical practice is adding new X9516 X-Fabric module, UCS PCI Mezz cards, and UCS X580p PCIe nodes to their existing X-Series chassis. Which two administrative actions must be taken before the X-Fabric module is added to the chassis? (Choose two.)
explanation: The UCS X9516 X-Fabric Module provides PCIe Gen5 connectivity between supported M8 compute nodes and X580p PCIe nodes. Before enabling that connectivity, the affected compute nodes must be powered down and equipped with the appropriate UCS PCI Gen5 mezzanine cards . Cisco identifies the UCSX-V5-PCIME rear mezzanine card as a required hardware component for X580p connectivity. The card provides PCIe Gen5 electrical lanes between each CPU and the X9516 X-Fabric modules. Cisco also specifies that companion compute-node host power must be off for insertion or removal operations involving X580p PCIe connectivity, and that X9516 modules must be installed before the X580p PCIe nodes are installed. Therefore, powering down the affected blades and installing their required PCI mezzanine cards are the appropriate preparatory actions. The IFMs provide normal UCS network connectivity and do not need to be powered off or disconnected from Fabric Interconnects merely to install the X-Fabric modules. Similarly, disconnecting the Device Connector is unrelated to physical PCIe fabric installation and would unnecessarily interrupt Intersight connectivity. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Deployment and Data Management — Cisco UCS X-Series GPU expansion, X-Fabric, PCIe connectivity, and hardware deployment.

stem: What is the process involved in workload scheduling for AI environments?
explanation: Workload scheduling determines where and when computational jobs execute by assigning workloads to available processing resources according to resource requirements, capacity, policies, priorities, and performance objectives. In AI environments, this commonly means allocating training, fine-tuning, or inference jobs to CPUs, GPUs, GPU memory, or groups of accelerator nodes so expensive computational resources remain efficiently utilized. Cisco's DCAI blueprint explicitly includes orchestration as an AI-environment component. Cisco material covering NVIDIA Run:ai also identifies scheduling and GPU orchestration as core AI workload-orchestration capabilities and describes infrastructure pooling and resource management designed to maximize compute efficiency. Therefore, assigning tasks to compute elements for optimized performance precisely describes workload scheduling. Option B concerns software licensing and compliance management. Option C is monitoring or telemetry aggregation, which can inform scheduling decisions but is not scheduling itself. Option D is a backup and recovery operation. Effective AI scheduling is particularly important because GPU resources are expensive and workloads vary significantly in duration and resource demand. A capable scheduler therefore improves accelerator utilization, reduces queueing, and coordinates workload placement across the available compute infrastructure. Study Guide Reference: 1.0 AI Fundamentals and Applications — 1.5.d Orchestration.

stem: How does RAG enhance the capabilities of LLMs?
explanation: Retrieval-Augmented Generation enhances an LLM by retrieving relevant information from external knowledge sources and incorporating that material into the context supplied to the model during generation. This permits a pretrained model to answer questions using organization-specific information without requiring its underlying model parameters to be retrained for every knowledge update. Cisco describes RAG as a technique that connects LLM applications to additional data sources, including internal repositories containing sensitive customer or business information. Cisco's enterprise RAG guidance specifically emphasizes using proprietary organizational data to ground responses in enterprise information. Therefore, providing access to proprietary data is the correct answer. Option A is incorrect because RAG does not eliminate ingestion, parsing, chunking, cleaning, embedding, or indexing requirements. Option B is too absolute: grounding can improve factual relevance but does not inherently remove model bias. Option D describes modification of model parameters, which is characteristic of training or fine-tuning rather than standard RAG retrieval. Cisco explicitly includes RAG as a required DCAI workload type, so candidates must distinguish retrieval- based augmentation from model training and fine-tuning. Study Guide Reference: 1.0 AI Fundamentals and Applications — 1.1.a RAG.

stem: Which type of Cisco Intersight profile, when deployed to fabric interconnects, includes the configuration settings for ports, VLANs, and VSANs?
explanation: A UCS Domain Profile provides the configuration model for a pair of Cisco UCS Fabric Interconnects operating in Intersight Managed Mode. Cisco explicitly states that the Domain Profile allows configuration of FI ports and port channels and defines the VLANs and VSANs used by the domain. This makes option C an exact match for the functionality described. The Domain Profile references reusable policies rather than embedding every setting directly. VLAN and VSAN policies are associated during the VLAN and VSAN configuration stage, Port Policies are assigned during port configuration, and additional management or compute-related domain policies are attached subsequently. When the Domain Profile is deployed, Intersight applies the assembled configuration to the assigned Fabric Interconnect domain. A Chassis Profile configures chassis-specific properties and cannot replace domain-level network configuration. A Server Profile configures an individual server's identity, boot configuration, vNICs, vHBAs, firmware, BIOS, storage, and similar server-specific characteristics. Unified Edge uses its own distributed edge management model and is not the FI configuration object in question. This distinction is fundamental in Intersight Managed Mode: Domain Profiles configure the Fabric Interconnect domain, while Server Profiles configure individual compute resources attached to that domain. stem: What describes inference traffic patterns in AI deployments?
explanation: Inference is the operational phase in which a trained AI model receives new input and produces predictions, classifications, generated content, or other decisions. Cisco explicitly identifies Inference as an AI/ML workload type in DCAI objective 1.1.c. Unlike model training, which is dominated by iterative computation over large datasets, inference commonly handles production requests and is highly sensitive to response latency and throughput. Cisco's AI POD design guidance states that inferencing workloads process live production traffic, often in real time, and evaluates them using metrics such as Time-to-First-Token, end-to-end request latency, inter-token latency, and requests per second. These characteristics directly support real-time decision making , making option C correct. Option A concerns storage architecture rather than inference behavior. Option B incorrectly describes model architecture simplification, which inference does not inherently perform. Option D is also incorrect because inference pipelines can still require preprocessing, normalization, tokenization, or transformation of incoming data. Study Guide Reference: 1.0 AI Fundamentals and Applications — 1.1 AI/ML workload types — 1.1.c Inference.

stem: A network engineer logs into Nexus Dashboard and sees an anomaly showing that a BGP peer connection has gone down. Next to the anomaly, a yellow bubble displays “Correlated.” What does Nexus Dashboard indicate by “Correlated” in this case?
explanation: In Cisco Nexus Dashboard, a correlated anomaly is a secondary condition that Nexus Dashboard has associated through cause-and-effect analysis with another anomaly identified as the probable root cause. Cisco's current documentation explicitly distinguishes root-cause anomalies from correlated anomalies: the root anomaly triggers additional symptoms, and those dependent symptoms are displayed as correlated events. For example, a physical or routing event may cause a downstream BGP session to fail. Rather than presenting each symptom as an independent failure, Nexus Dashboard analyzes relationships involving interfaces, devices, protocols, and timestamps. The BGP peer-down condition can therefore appear as correlated when a higher-level underlying anomaly explains it. Option A incorrectly associates correlation with user-account activity. Option B describes repetition across several devices, which is not what the correlation indicator means. Option D refers generally to impact analysis rather than the specific root-cause relationship communicated by the label. This feature reduces troubleshooting time because engineers can focus first on the root anomaly. Cisco specifically notes that resolving the underlying root cause should also resolve the anomalies correlated with that condition. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — Nexus Dashboard assurance, anomaly correlation, root-cause identification, and troubleshooting.

stem: Which aspect of rapid provisioning supports a scalable workload execution in an AI infrastructure?
explanation: Rapid provisioning supports scalability by reducing the time required to make compute, GPU, networking, storage, and orchestration resources available for workloads. The most appropriate description is therefore the efficient launch of computational platforms . When new AI capacity can be provisioned consistently and quickly, organizations can expand training environments, increase inference capacity, respond to workload bursts, and introduce additional accelerator resources without lengthy manual configuration. Cisco's DCAI objectives explicitly cover orchestration as a component of AI environments and require candidates to evaluate infrastructure scalability. Cisco also emphasizes that AI infrastructure must scale to accommodate changing workloads and that cloud-oriented infrastructure offers rapid access to computational resources when demand changes. Option A introduces fragmented management, which generally increases operational complexity. Option B restricts connectivity and therefore conflicts with scalable distributed AI execution. Option C explicitly delays resource availability and is the opposite of rapid provisioning. The architectural objective is to make infrastructure consumption repeatable and automated. Efficient provisioning allows the underlying platform to expand at the pace demanded by GPU-intensive training and production inference rather than becoming an operational bottleneck. Study Guide Reference: 1.0 AI Fundamentals and Applications — 1.5.d Orchestration; AI infrastructure scalability concepts.

stem: Which network design approach should be used to build a high-performance, nonblocking AI/ML data center fabric that supports 64 fully equipped UCS C885A nodes and provides the lowest possible latency and lossless Ethernet?
explanation: A rail-optimized topology is specifically engineered for large GPU clusters where collective communication performance and minimum inter-GPU latency are critical. In a rail-optimized design, corresponding GPU/NIC interfaces across compute nodes attach to the same rail switch. This allows communication between GPUs of the same rank to remain on a single leaf or rail switch whenever possible, eliminating unnecessary spine traversal and reducing network hops. Cisco's AI/ML networking guidance gives a directly applicable design example: a rail-optimized, nonblocking architecture connecting 512 GPUs in 64 nodes, with eight GPUs per node . The design uses eight rail/leaf switches and four spine switches and maintains nonblocking bandwidth while optimizing GPU collective communication. Cisco explicitly states that rail-optimized design is recommended for NVIDIA GPU environments. A conventional leaf-spine architecture can certainly provide high performance and nonblocking bandwidth, but option C is more specific to the requirement for the lowest possible GPU-to-GPU latency at this scale. Flat Layer 2 does not provide the required scalable fabric architecture, while a traditional three-tier model introduces additional hops and potential oversubscription. Study Guide Reference: 2.0 AI Infrastructure Components and Architecture — 2.1 Evaluate network deployment based on bandwidth, latency, redundancy, scalability, and security.

stem: An Intersight administrator plans to deploy new server solutions to several small branch offices across the country. Each location needs at least one chassis. The servers must have redundant CPUs, memory, and 200 Gbps of unified fabric connectivity per compute node. Which hybrid AI compute solution meets the requirements?
explanation: Cisco UCS X-Series Direct is specifically designed for edge, retail, remote-office, and branch-office environments that require the operational characteristics of UCS without deploying separate top-of-rack Fabric Interconnect appliances. It combines the UCS X9508 chassis with integrated UCS 9108 100G Fabric Interconnect modules and supports centralized management through Cisco Intersight. The decisive requirement is 200 Gbps of unified fabric connectivity per compute node . Cisco documents that two UCS 9108 100G Fabric Interconnect modules provide a total of 200 Gbps per compute node. The solution can support up to eight compute nodes per chassis and is explicitly positioned for remote and branch- office deployments. The S3260 is primarily a storage-intensive UCS platform and does not represent the required branch-oriented modular compute architecture. Unified Edge is purpose-built for edge locations, but the specific 200-Gbps- per-compute-node requirement aligns directly with X-Series Direct. The C885A M8 is a high-density rack server for GPU-intensive AI workloads rather than a chassis solution optimized for these branch deployment requirements. Study Guide Reference: 2.0 AI Infrastructure Components and Architecture — 2.2 compute scalability and redundancy; 2.5 hybrid AI deployment.

stem: A corporate network administrator manages a HyperFabric AI environment and wants to receive email notifications about assertions in the fabric. The administrator sets up a recipient email endpoint under the notification endpoints in the controller, but notifications are not received. Which two configurations cause the issue? (Choose two.)
explanation: Configuring an email address as a notification endpoint is not sufficient by itself. Cisco Nexus Hyperfabric requires the recipient endpoint to undergo email verification . After an email endpoint is created, Hyperfabric sends a verification code; the administrator must enter that code and confirm that the endpoint status is verified and active. An unverified address therefore causes the condition described in option B. The endpoint must also be associated with a notification policy . Cisco documents that assertion notifications are configured by selecting one or more fabrics and one or more notification endpoints in the notification policy. If the relevant fabric and the newly created email endpoint are not paired in the policy, assertion messages are not sent to that address. This makes option C correct. Options A and E incorrectly assume that Hyperfabric directly uses the organization's own email server. Nexus Hyperfabric provides the notification service through its controller architecture. Option D similarly does not represent the required notification configuration described by Cisco. The correct operational workflow is therefore: create the email endpoint, complete verification, then associate the desired fabric and endpoint through the notification policy. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — Hyperfabric monitoring, assertions, notification endpoints, and notification policies.

stem: An engineer must monitor congestion, flow latency, and traffic drops using Cisco Nexus Dashboard and chooses to use the Traffic Analytics feature. Which Nexus Dashboard feature is automatically disabled when Traffic Analytics is enabled?
explanation: Traffic Analytics and Flow Telemetry are mutually exclusive flow-collection modes within Cisco Nexus Dashboard. Cisco's current Nexus Dashboard documentation identifies both under Flow Collection settings and states that Flow Telemetry must be disabled at the fabric level before Traffic Analytics can be enabled. Traffic Analytics automatically discovers services and visualizes conversations based primarily on Layer 4 information. It provides visibility into network characteristics such as congestion, latency, and drops, which directly matches the monitoring requirements in the scenario. Cisco's Nexus Dashboard Insights guidance likewise states that if Flow Telemetry is already active, it must first be disabled for the relevant sites before Traffic Analytics is selected. Delta Analysis is an assurance/comparison capability and is not the mutually exclusive collection mode described here. Connectivity Analysis performs reachability and path-oriented diagnostics. SNMP traps remain a separate event-notification mechanism and are not displaced by Traffic Analytics. The operational distinction matters because Traffic Analytics and Flow Telemetry use different approaches to flow collection and analysis. An administrator cannot simply enable both collection modes simultaneously and expect them to operate in parallel on the same fabric configuration. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Operations and Troubleshooting — Nexus Dashboard monitoring, telemetry, congestion analysis, latency, and packet-drop visibility.

stem: A company is building a network fabric for an AI training cluster that will train large language models. The cluster includes 256 GPUs distributed across 32 servers. Security requirements mandate isolation between different training projects and allowing shared access to a central storage system. Which approach provides the required security isolation and maintains optimal performance for GPU-to-GPU communication?
explanation: VXLAN EVPN provides scalable logical segmentation without requiring physically separate fabrics. Separate VXLAN Network Identifiers can isolate individual AI training projects, while Cisco's Group Policy Option adds a security group identifier to the VXLAN header and enables granular microsegmentation through security-group policies. This makes it possible to isolate tenant or project traffic while selectively allowing access to common services such as centralized storage. Cisco specifically describes GPO as supporting microsegmentation within VXLAN EVPN fabrics and granular traffic control between application segments. This approach preserves a high-performance shared fabric, avoiding the operational complexity and resource inefficiency of constructing physically separate networks for every project. Cisco also positions VXLAN EVPN as an architecture for AI/ML environments requiring segmentation, secure multitenancy, and scalable high-throughput communication. Option A provides strong isolation but wastes switching resources and complicates shared-storage connectivity. Option C relies on conventional VLAN boundaries and centralized router ACL enforcement, introducing scaling and potentially additional forwarding constraints. stem: A data center is deploying an AI infrastructure for LLM training and model inference. This infrastructure requires high GPU density, low-latency interconnects, and the ability to scale compute resources. When considering the Cisco UCS C885A M8 Rack Server for the deployment, which design aspect is the most critical for achieving optimal performance and scalability in this environment?
explanation: Selecting and correctly engineering the Nexus fabric is the most important option for achieving scalable AI performance because distributed LLM training depends heavily on communication among GPUs located in different servers. The C885A M8 provides eight high-performance GPUs and high-speed NICs, but cluster- level performance depends on whether the network can transport collective-communication traffic at high bandwidth with extremely low latency and negligible packet loss. Cisco AI reference architectures use dedicated, nonblocking backend fabrics based on Cisco Nexus switching for GPU-to-GPU RoCEv2 traffic. Cisco specifically applies rail-optimized designs, PFC, ECN, high-speed Ethernet, and nonblocking leaf-spine connectivity to preserve collective communication efficiency as GPU clusters scale. Option B overemphasizes host CPU cores. LLM training on the C885A is primarily GPU accelerated, and additional CPU capacity does not compensate for a congested inter-node fabric. Option C is essential for availability but does not directly optimize distributed training throughput or scalability. Option D would actively undermine workload capability because adequate host memory is important for data preprocessing, orchestration, caching, and other AI operations. Therefore, the network fabric's topology, bandwidth, congestion-control behavior, and latency are central to realizing the performance of a multi-node C885A deployment. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Components and Architecture — evaluate network and compute deployments based on bandwidth, latency, scalability, GPU characteristics, and workload requirements.

stem: What is a primary behavior that occurs during the model training stage of the AI lifecycle?
explanation: The defining computational activity of model training is the iterative adjustment of the model's trainable parameters—principally weights and biases —to reduce an objective or loss function. During training, input examples are processed through the model, prediction error is calculated, gradients are derived, and an optimization algorithm updates parameters. Repetition across batches and epochs gradually produces a model that captures useful patterns and relationships in the training data. Cisco identifies Training as a specific AI/ML workload type and separately requires knowledge of the overall AI lifecycle. Cisco's AI/ML operations guidance describes model training as the process through which a model learns patterns, features, representations, and relationships from data and places training before deployment and production operation. Option A represents deployment or application integration after training. Option B normally belongs to problem definition and project-planning stages before model development. Option D is a production- monitoring activity used to determine whether a deployed model's behavior has degraded or changed because incoming data or underlying relationships have shifted. Therefore, C identifies the central learning mechanism occurring during the training stage. Study Guide Reference: 1.0 AI Fundamentals and Applications — 1.1.b Training; 1.2 Describe the AI lifecycle.

stem: Which result is provided through image recognition using AI?
explanation: Image recognition is a computer-vision application in which an AI model processes digital imagery and identifies meaningful visual content. Depending on the model and use case, the output can include image classifications, detected objects, faces, locations, labels, bounding boxes, or other semantic information describing what appears in the image. Therefore, detection and labeling of visual elements from digital sources is the correct result. Cisco identifies computer vision as an established AI/ML workload and has used image-recognition techniques in technologies where models learn to identify objects despite variations in position and orientation. The DCAI exam blueprint requires candidates to understand AI use cases, making the distinction between computer-vision workloads and unrelated infrastructure functions important. Option A is a security and compliance operation involving data anonymization. Option C is an infrastructure scheduling function generally performed by orchestration or management systems. Option D belongs to network control-plane and forwarding behavior and has no direct relationship to image recognition. The key examination principle is that image recognition transforms unstructured visual input into meaningful classifications or detections that can subsequently drive automated decisions or analytics. Study Guide Reference: 1.0 AI Fundamentals and Applications — 1.3 Describe AI use cases.

stem: A medical company has existing third-party AI servers and NVMe storage, but they want to purchase Cisco network switches with a cloud managed feature for simplicity. Which solution best meets the requirements?
explanation: The organization already owns third-party AI servers and NVMe storage, so it requires a network-centric AI fabric rather than a Cisco full-stack solution that bundles UCS compute. Cisco Nexus Hyperfabric supports bring-your-own infrastructure scenarios while providing cloud-based design, deployment, management, telemetry, and lifecycle operations. The licensing distinction is critical. Cisco's current Nexus Hyperfabric documentation defines Essentials primarily for general-purpose fabrics, whereas Premier is the entitlement tier designed for AI fabrics. Premier includes AI-specific functionality such as alignment with NVIDIA reference architectures, adaptive routing support, AI-validated blueprints, automated lossless backend networking, and monitoring between switches and servers. Option A uses the correct bring-your-own model but the wrong subscription tier for an AI fabric. Option D represents the full-stack Hyperfabric AI model, which includes Cisco UCS servers and therefore conflicts with the requirement to retain existing third-party compute. Option C does not match the requested Cisco 6000 Series cloud-managed Hyperfabric architecture. Accordingly, BYO AI Hyperfabric using Cisco 6000 Series switches with the Premier entitlement satisfies both reuse of existing infrastructure and AI-specific cloud-managed networking. Study Guide Reference: 3.3.c Hyperfabric — deploy AI-ready fabrics using Cisco orchestration tools.

stem: A company deploys a Cisco UCS environment to host AI inferencing workloads that demand low latency, high throughput, and efficient resource utilization. Which set of actions must be taken to deploy a high-performance fabric within the Cisco UCS infrastructure?
explanation: A high-performance Cisco UCS architecture normally uses redundant fabric interconnects to provide both high availability and aggregated bandwidth. Cisco documentation describes Fabric Interconnects as typically deployed as a pair, integrating UCS components into a highly available management and connectivity domain. Modern UCS X-Series connectivity can provide up to 200 Gbps aggregate unified-fabric bandwidth per compute node through dual 100-Gbps paths. Option D therefore aligns with UCS architecture: dual fabrics eliminate the single point of failure associated with one Fabric Interconnect, while 100-Gbps connectivity supports high-throughput AI inference workloads. Port channels on uplinks provide bandwidth aggregation and link-level resiliency toward the upstream data center network. Option A incorrectly limits the Fabric Interconnect to management traffic; UCS unified fabric carries production Ethernet, storage, and management-related connectivity. Option B bypasses the integrated UCS fabric architecture and unnecessarily separates management onto Catalyst infrastructure. Option C introduces both a single point of failure and a severe bandwidth constraint by using one FI and 10-Gbps links. For AI inference, where throughput and deterministic latency directly influence application performance, redundant high-speed fabric design is the appropriate implementation. Study Guide Reference: 3.0 AI Infrastructure Deployment and Data Management — 3.2 Configure high- performance compute and storage using Cisco UCS; 3.2.d LAN connectivity and vNIC policies.

stem: A server administrator must monitor the performance and utilization of GPUs in Cisco UCS servers running AI workloads. Which two metrics must be used in Cisco Intersight to accomplish these goals? (Choose two.)
explanation: The uploaded source marks C and D . GPU Memory Utilization in option D is clearly relevant: GPU memory pressure is a critical accelerator metric because model weights, activations, KV caches, tensors, and training state consume GPU-attached memory. Cisco AI monitoring material explicitly includes GPU memory utilization among the telemetry used for AI infrastructure visibility. Option C, Active CPU Utilization , is useful as a supporting performance metric because AI workloads can become CPU-bound during data preprocessing, tokenization, orchestration, input-pipeline execution, or host- to-device preparation. A CPU bottleneck can therefore leave GPUs underutilized even when sufficient accelerator capacity exists. However, the question as written has a notable construction issue: Cisco documentation treats GPU utilization itself as a principal metric for evaluating accelerator utilization, but that metric is absent from the available answer choices. Cisco current material explicitly identifies GPU utilization and GPU memory utilization as AI monitoring measurements. Therefore, CD is retained because it is the answer supplied by the source , but the technically ideal metric pair would be GPU Utilization + GPU Memory Utilization if GPU Utilization were offered. stem: A nationwide grocery chain has deployed Unified Edge to all its locations. Each store has 10 or more surveillance cameras that write approximately 1 Gb per hour. The surveillance retention policy requires maintaining 2 weeks of recording per camera. Which type of cost-effective centralized storage solution must be evaluated with Unified Edge devices to adhere to this policy?
explanation: The surveillance workload creates a substantial persistent-capacity requirement across every location. Even at the stated minimum of ten cameras, each store generates approximately 240 GB per day and roughly 3.36 TB over fourteen days before considering filesystem overhead, redundancy, additional cameras, or growth. A scalable IP-based shared-storage architecture is therefore the appropriate option. Cisco Unified Edge is designed around integrated high-speed Ethernet networking and supports network- accessible storage through standard IP mechanisms. Cisco's validated Unified Edge guidance describes network storage using protocols such as NFS and iSCSI , while explicitly noting that Fibre Channel is not validated in that design. Unified Edge also supports software-defined and distributed storage architectures carried over its Ethernet infrastructure. Fibre Channel would introduce specialized SAN adapters, switches, cabling, and operational complexity that are generally inappropriate for a cost-sensitive, highly distributed retail edge. InfiniBand is optimized for specialized high-performance computing rather than economical video retention. Local storage could hold surveillance data at each store, but the question explicitly requires a centralized storage solution and long-term capacity that can be managed across locations. IP-based shared storage therefore provides the best combination of scalability, standardization, cost efficiency, and Unified Edge compatibility. stem: A network team is configuring quality of service (QoS) for RoCEv2 traffic on a VXLAN fabric. The team must ensure that congestion notification packets (CNP) generated by storage targets are never dropped in the network, as these packets are critical for congestion control feedback. How must CNP packets be handled in the QoS configuration to ensure reliable delivery?
explanation: Congestion Notification Packets are control-feedback messages used by RoCEv2 congestion-management mechanisms. When a receiving endpoint observes an ECN-marked packet, it generates a CNP toward the sender, instructing the transmitting endpoint to reduce its transmission rate. Losing these packets would delay congestion response and allow queues to continue building. Cisco's validated RoCEv2-over-VXLAN design explicitly states that CNP packets use DSCP 48 and are classified into a high-priority queue . In Cisco's example, ordinary RoCEv2 traffic is mapped to QoS group 3, while CNP is mapped to QoS group 7. Cisco further states that the high-priority classification ensures that CNP packets are not dropped in the network. Traffic shaping in option A would regulate CNP transmission rather than guarantee timely feedback. Option C places CNP in the same potentially congested queue as the data traffic that generated the congestion, defeating the purpose of reliable feedback. Option D is also incorrect because PFC is intended to protect a lossless data priority; CNP itself should be forwarded through a high-priority queue and should not depend on pause behavior. Study Guide Reference: AI Infrastructure Deployment and Data Management — RoCEv2, ECN, CNP, QoS classification, and congestion management.

stem: An organization deploys a new AI training fabric that uses RoCEv2 for GPU communication. The network architect designs the QoS configuration to ensure reliable RDMA transport and must meet these requirements: Support 256 GPU servers with RDMA connectivity. Prevent any packet loss that causes RDMA connection failures. Maintain consistent low-latency communication with a target of less than 10 microseconds. Use industry-standard protocols and configurations. Which configuration ensures that RoCEv2 operates as a lossless transport?
explanation: Priority Flow Control is a foundational mechanism used to provide lossless Ethernet behavior for RoCEv2. PFC operates on individual Ethernet priorities and allows a congested receiver or switch to pause transmission for the affected priority while permitting traffic in other classes to continue. Cisco's AI networking guidance explicitly states that PFC is enabled for RoCEv2 traffic to prevent packet drops caused by congestion. This characteristic is critical for RDMA workloads because packet loss can trigger retransmission behavior and significantly degrade GPU collective communication performance. In an AI backend fabric, RoCEv2 is normally placed in a no-drop QoS class with PFC configured for that traffic class. ECN is commonly used alongside PFC to provide proactive congestion signaling, but PFC is the mechanism that directly prevents loss when buffers approach critical utilization. Traffic shaping in option A may moderate burst rates but does not establish lossless transport. A high DSCP marking in option C provides classification and forwarding preference, not loss prevention. Weighted fair queuing in option D allocates scheduling bandwidth but also does not guarantee that packets will not be discarded during congestion. Study Guide Reference: 3.1.a Congestion control mechanisms — PFC, ECN, ETS; 3.1.b RoCE/RoCEv2; 3.1.c QoS.
